review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the declarations against their uses elsewhere in Mathlib. The clearest case is the pair of duplicated op/unop constructions: `terminalOpOfInitial`/`terminalUnopOfInitial` and `IsInitial.op`/`IsInitial.unop`. I grepped for uses of the older names; they appear in several files (CommAlgCat, Sites, AlgebraicGeometry, Terminal.lean), so consolidation would need to rewrite or deprecate those uses. I did not find a documented reason to keep both. The other declarations I checked (`isTerminalEquivUnique`, `isLimitEquivIsTerminalOfIsEmpty`, `InitialMonoClass`, `coneOfDiagramInitial`) looked like distinct or specialised concepts, so I did not report them. I did not check whether the `to_dual` pairs are fully symmetric beyond the op/unop declarations.

findings.declaration: terminalOpOfInitial / terminalUnopOfInitial (and duals initialOpOfTerminal / initialUnopOfTerminal) duplicate IsInitial.op / IsInitial.unop (and duals)
findings.excerpt: def terminalOpOfInitial {X : C} (t : IsInitial X) : IsTerminal (Opposite.op X) where
findings.problem: The file defines the same two constructions twice under different names. `terminalOpOfInitial` and `IsInitial.op` both turn `IsInitial X` into `IsTerminal (op X)`, with identical docstrings. `terminalUnopOfInitial` and `IsInitial.unop` both turn `IsInitial X` for `X : Cᵒᵖ` into `IsTerminal X.unop`, also with identical docstrings. Each pair has its own `to_dual` counterpart, so four near-identical declarations carry the same content. The two spellings are used interchangeably across the library. Terminal.lean and the Sites, AlgebraicGeometry and CommAlgCat files use the old names, while newer code can use the dot-notation versions. This leaves two competing APIs for one concept, and users must know both.
findings.proposed_change: Keep one family, preferably the dot-notation `IsInitial.op`/`IsInitial.unop`/`IsTerminal.op`/`IsTerminal.unop`. Define the old names as deprecated aliases, or migrate their uses. Alternatively, keep the old names and define the dot-notation ones as `abbrev`s or aliases of them. In either case there should be one implementation, not two.
findings.benefit: This removes duplicated definitions and `to_dual` pairs, and gives readers one canonical name per construction. It also avoids terms that are propositionally equal but syntactically different, which can cause rewriting and unification friction in the downstream uses.
